meta.description: Retrieve records from NCBI databases with Bio.Entrez EFetch and ESummary.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: Current live outputs are labelled as database records and the Skill distinguishes metadata retrieval from full-record retrieval.

practice_boundaries.detail: ClinVar and dbSNP examples report record fields without personal diagnostic or treatment inference.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh executions covered the actual EFetch/ESummary modes, response sniffing, bytes decoding, XML/ElementTree choice, and history-server path.

code_usability.detail: Every current shipped example and supporting-script route completed in the private re-audit runtime.

functional_suitability.note: Current source covers versioned sequences, metadata, PubMed, history, SRA, taxonomy, and variant records.

reliability.note: Response-prefix guards, type decoding, mixed-ID warning, and source scripts handle the major silent-failure patterns.

performance_context.note: ESummary batching and history-server retrieval explicitly avoid oversized and needlessly expensive requests.

agent_usability.note: The record-versus-metadata triage and database-specific rettype matrix are explicit.

human_usability.note: Failure modes identify silent empty, HTML, schema, GI, and WGS conditions with recoveries.

security.note: No credential is hard-coded and no untrusted execution surface was found.

maintainability.note: Focused scripts and references are separated, although the documented cds_proteins helper could close its EFetch handle explicitly.

agent_specific.note: The source gives precise decision boundaries and safe escapes for XML schema and large-result workflows.

inputs.label: Current version-pinned GenBank, CDS, batch, and gbwithparts example
inputs.execution_note: Executed examples/fetch_sequences.py in a temporary directory: NM_007294.4 was 7,088 nt with one CDS; NC_000913.3 returned 4,318 translated CDS; all three versioned accessions returned; gbwithparts returned 55,515 bytes.

inputs.label: Current bulk nucleotide and PubMed summaries
inputs.execution_note: Executed examples/fetch_summaries.py: four nucleotide and three PubMed docsums parsed; current measured EFetch/ESummary payload ratio was 47.3x.

inputs.label: Current PubMed MEDLINE and XML example
inputs.execution_note: Executed examples/fetch_pubmed.py: MEDLINE records returned titles and MeSH terms; XML returned title, journal, seven MeSH descriptors, zero grants, and PMC9093120 without StringElement indexing failure.

inputs.label: Current ClinVar VCV ElementTree script
inputs.execution_note: Executed scripts/variant_records.py clinvar 4887763: ElementTree returned VCV000005107 and its stated Pathogenic classification without diagnostic inference.

inputs.label: Current history-server FASTA script
inputs.execution_note: Executed scripts/history_fetch.py on NM_007294.4[Accession] into a temporary file: one requested record produced a 7,385-byte FASTA with one header.

inputs.label: Current dbSNP record path without clinical overreach
inputs.execution_note: Executed scripts/variant_records.py snp 429358: parsed chromosome 19 and APOE metadata through ElementTree, reporting only source metadata rather than a patient conclusion.

inputs.label: Current SRA bytes/error-body and taxonomy routes
inputs.execution_note: Executed the current documented SRA runinfo pattern using live UID 8 for SRR000001: seven rows parsed after bytes decoding; taxonomy 9606 returned Homo sapiens; the HTML error-body sentinel was rejected before CSV parsing.

key_strengths: The provenance re-audit executed every shipped current route at the requested commit in a newly isolated audit worktree.
Version-pinned sequences, history-server retrieval, XML/ElementTree parsing, and response-prefix guards all produced current live evidence.
Variant routes preserve the necessary boundary between record metadata and clinical inference.

recommendations.title: Close the documented cds_proteins EFetch handle explicitly
recommendations.problem: The SKILL.md helper materializes all FASTA records but does not explicitly close its EFetch handle.
recommendations.root_cause: The inline convenience example returns list(SeqIO.parse(h, 'fasta')) directly.
recommendations.fix: Read the records, close the handle, then return the list, or use a context-managed handle.
